title: Region-aware routing authoring cheatsheet
content:
Purpose and scope
-----------------
This is a concise authoring and validation cheatsheet for writing region-aware routing policy files, validating them locally/CI, and rolling them out via the control plane. It is intended for platform engineers and API owners who need to author routing rules that: (a) route requests by region/latency/capacity tier, (b) include graceful fallbacks, and (c) can be validated and staged safely across regions.

Why a separate cheatsheet?
- Existing routing docs are high-level. This is a practical set of patterns, a compact schema reference, and rollout playbook optimized for iterative authoring in Drive and CI.
- Emphasizes safety checks, preflight simulation, and automated validation.

Design principles (short)
- Explicit intent: rules must be readable; avoid magic defaults.
- Fail-open vs fail-closed: prefer fail-open for user-facing latency-sensitive paths, fail-closed for sensitive/regulatory flows.
- Region affinity first, then capacity, then cost.
- Prefer deterministic routing for A/B trials and canaries (explicit weights).
- Keep fallbacks simple and auditable.

Quick glossary
- control plane: Redwood’s API that stores routing rules and serves them to the runtime.
- rule: a single routing configuration unit that maps incoming predicates to backends.
- backend: a model+deployment target (hosted/dedicated/private) with region metadata.
- policy: an ordered list of rules applied to requests.

Core schema (compact JSON reference)
Note: this is canonical minimal schema used by the control plane validator. Fields not shown here are optional metadata.

{
  "policy_id": "string (slug)",
  "description": "string",
  "version": "semver",
  "match": {
    "principal": "optional string e.g. customer_id or api_key tag",
    "attributes": { "region": "eu-west-1|us-east-1|*", "product": "chat|embedding|rerank" },
    "predicate": "optional expression (see query language below)"
  },
  "routes": [
    {
      "id": "string (unique)",
      "weight": "int (0-100) default 100",
      "backend_ref": "string (deployment id)",
      "region": "string or list e.g. [us-east-1, us-west-2]",
      "min_capacity_tokens_per_sec": "int optional",
      "max_latency_ms": "int optional",
      "qualifiers": ["quantization=8bit", "gpu_type=A100"],
      "fallback": "backend_ref or null"
    }
  ],
  "rollout": {
    "strategy": "canary|progressive|instant",
    "canary": { "regions": ["us-east-1"], "percent": 5, "duration_minutes": 30 },
    "progressive": { "steps": [{"percent": 10, "duration_minutes": 60}, {"percent": 50, "duration_minutes": 60}], "concurrency": "per-region|global" },
    "auto_rollback": { "enabled": true, "latency_threshold_ms": 200, "error_rate_threshold_pct": 1.0, "lookback_minutes": 5 }
  },
  "metadata": { "author": "string", "contact": "email" }
}

Predicate/query language (brief)
- Simple boolean expressions on attributes: region == "eu-west-1" && product == "chat"
- Support for IP/CIDR, header lookups, token attributes, and numeric comparisons.
- Keep predicates simple; complex logic should be encapsulated in a preprocessor service.

Example: multi-region rule with fallback and weighted canary
{
  "policy_id": "policy-rl-2025-voice-api",
  "description": "Route voice-api by region with US-EAST canary and fallback to hosted-generic when dedicated saturated.",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "match": { "attributes": { "product": "voice" } },
  "routes": [
    { "id": "r1-us-east-primary", "weight": 90, "backend_ref": "dedicated-us-east-01", "region": "us-east-1", "min_capacity_tokens_per_sec": 10000, "qualifiers": ["gpu_type=A100"], "fallback": "hosted-us" },
    { "id": "r2-eu-primary", "weight": 10, "backend_ref": "dedicated-eu-02", "region": "eu-west-1", "min_capacity_tokens_per_sec": 8000, "fallback": "hosted-eu" }
  ],
  "rollout": { "strategy": "canary", "canary": { "regions": ["us-east-1"], "percent": 5, "duration_minutes": 20 }, "auto_rollback": { "enabled": true, "latency_threshold_ms": 150, "error_rate_threshold_pct": 0.8, "lookback_minutes": 3 } }
}

Validation checklist (local + CI)
1) Schema: run control-plane schema validator (npm package: redwood-routing-lint) — fails on missing fields, invalid weights, duplicate route ids.
2) Referential: backends referenced must exist in the inventory API (call /inventory/backends/:id). CI should mock or assert presence.
3) Capacity sanity: min_capacity_tokens_per_sec should not exceed declared backend capacity.
4) Region coverage: if routes are region-specific ensure there’s at least one fallback reachable globally.
5) Predicate safety: disallow regexes above a complexity threshold; ensure predicates are constant-time.
6) Rollout viability: canary percent > 0 and <= 10 by default; progressive steps must increase.
7) Security: policies touching "private" or "on-prem" backends must have explicit approvals linked in metadata.
8) Integration smoke: CI should run a request-level simulator (see next section) to validate observed weighted splits.

Local preflight simulator (how to use)
- Purpose: quickly validate routing outcomes for a policy. Simple Python script (r-route-sim) takes policy JSON and simulates N requests from regions/attributes, then reports the distribution and detects unreachable fallbacks.
- Smoke tests to include in CI: 1000 simulated requests per region, assert weighted distribution within +/-5% for >50 samples.

Rollout mechanics (playbook)
1) Author policy in draft branch in git (policy files live in infra/routing/policies).
2) Run redwood-routing-lint locally and run simulator. Attach simulation output to PR.
3) Push PR -> CI runs: schema lint, inventory ref-check, smoke simulation.
4) After PR approval, create a control-plane release (POST /control-plane/policies with preview=true).
5) Preview environment: control plane computes an evaluation plan and runs simulation against recent telemetry. Verify latency & error predictions.
6) Start rollout: choose strategy (canary recommended for cross-region changes). Stage by region: "nearest" region first, then adjacent regions, then global.
7) Monitor: Dashboard shows per-route latency, errors, and token throughput. If auto_rollback criteria hit, control plane rolls back to previous stable version.
8) Post-rollout: mark policy as stable, update metadata with rollout notes (duration, incidents, observed latencies).

Operational knobs and recommendations
- Canary percent: default 5% (never > 10% for first 24 hours).
- Lookback windows: 1m/5m/15m support; use 5m for automated decisions.
- Health signals: prefer combined metric of p95 latency and error rate; do not base rollback solely on p50.
- Cost-aware routing: include optional "cost_budget" per policy to gate high-cost backends.

Failure modes and mitigation
- Backend mismatch: validation fails; stop rollout.
- Silent degradation (latency slowly increases): tune auto_rollback lookback to 15m for gradual regressions; manual intervention required.
- Region partition: ensure fallback route is reachable via multi-region hosted-backend.

Authoring tips and common patterns
- Prefer explicit route ids with a consistent naming convention: team-product-region-purpose (e.g., platform-embed-eu-primary).
- Keep qualifiers conservative: listing exact GPU types reduces flexibility—use class names when possible (gpu_class=A100-like).
- For global products, include a small global hosted route with weight 1 to guarantee request completion during outages.
- For regulatory-sensitive customers, include an explicit "legal_jurisdiction" attribute and gating rule that forces private backends.

Open questions / TODOs
- How should we express multi-tenant quotas in the policy schema? (ticketed as JIRA-INFR-4990)
- Validate predicate expression language in the community; consider switching to CEL for consistency (pros/cons in Confluence).
- Add standard library of predicate macros (e.g., region_in_eu, is_enterprise) and a macro registry.

Appendix: minimal lint commands and example CI snippet
- Local lint: npx redwood-routing-lint validate policy.json
- Inventory check (local curl): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://inventory.internal/api/backends/dedicated-us-east-01
- CI YAML snippet (simplified):
  - name: Lint routing policy
    run: npx redwood-routing-lint validate infra/routing/policies/*.json
  - name: Simulate policy
    run: python3 tools/r-route-sim.py infra/routing/policies/policy-rl-2025-voice-api.json --samples 1000 --assert-weight-delta 0.05

Notes to self (author)
- Keep this doc short and pragmatic. Move long rationale to confluence.
- After initial adoption, fold this into the control-plane authoring guide and link from Console policy UI.

Change history
- 2024-09-18 initial draft (Lena)
- 2025-01-10 added simulator guidance and CI snippets (Ravi)
- 2025-06-04 clarified auto_rollback thresholds and canary guidance (Aisha)

End of cheatsheet
